messages.text: Internationals take shock lead over USA into singles after late drama

metadata.summary: The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles.
metadata.content: Presidents Cup: International Team take historic 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into Sunday singles and chase Medinah win | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Presidents Cup: International Team take historic 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into Sunday singles and chase Medinah win A tied afternoon foursomes sessions gave the International Team a three-point lead into the final day at Medinah; Internationals need five points from the Sunday singles to claim just their second Presidents Cup win ever; watch the Sunday singles live from 4.30pm on Sky Sports Golf Ali Stafford Senior Sports Journalist Sunday 27 September 2026 00:55, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from Saturday's double session at the Presidents Cup, where the Internationals continue to lead on away soil The International Team moved another step closer to a historic Presidents Cup win on American soil by taking a 10.5-7.5 lead over Team USA into the Sunday singles. Geoff Ogilvy's side held a four-point advantage after the first two days at Medinah Country Club, following their historic foursomes sessions sweep on Friday, then added 1.5 points from four matches during a tight Saturday fourballs session. Team USA captain Brandt Snedeker benched world No 1 Scottie Scheffler for the afternoon foursomes, where they threatened their own session sweep after grabbing the early lead in all four matches. messages.text: Keane disagrees with Gordon: There is a gap between Spain and England

metadata.summary: Roy Keane disagreed with Anthony Gordon's assessment that England are at the same level as Spain after the World Cup winners came from behind to beat Thomas Tuchel's side 3-2 in their Nations League opener.
metadata.content: England 2-3 Spain: Anthony Gordon and Roy Keane disagree over gap between Three Lions and world champions | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England 2-3 Spain: Anthony Gordon and Roy Keane disagree over gap between Three Lions and world champions World Cup winners Spain pounced on basic errors from England's Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly for their first two goals, while Thomas Tuchel's side failed to capitalise on their dominance with Harry Kane's missed penalty proving to be a turning point at Wembley Sunday 27 September 2026 00:30, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Rob Dorsett and Pete Smith rate the England players' performances in the game against Spain. Roy Keane disagreed with Anthony Gordon's assessment that England are at the same level as Spain after the World Cup winners came from behind to beat Thomas Tuchel's side 3-2 in their Nations League opener. Spain extend their unbeaten run to 39 games with the win at Wembley, but the game could have had a very different outcome had Harry Kane not missed a second-half penalty after he headed England 2-1 in front before the break. The momentum shifted in Spain's favour after Kane's slip, with Alex Baena equalising off the bench before setting up the winner, scored by fellow substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who broke England hearts in the Euro 2024 final. messages.text: Fury: There's a one per cent chance of AJ fight happening

metadata.summary: Tyson Fury has asserted that there is a "one per cent" chance of his fight against Anthony Joshua going ahead.
metadata.content: Fury vs Joshua: Tyson Fury puts chances of mammoth all-British heavyweight clash vs Anthony Joshua going ahead at one per cent | Boxing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Fury vs Joshua: Tyson Fury puts chances of mammoth all-British heavyweight clash vs Anthony Joshua going ahead at one per cent Tyson Fury has claimed that there is now a "one per cent" chance of his fight against Anthony Joshua going ahead; Fury has cast further doubt on the all-British heavyweight fight in an interview on his YouTube channel Sunday 27 September 2026 00:47, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury says there is 1% chance of this fight actually taking place with Anthony Joshua. Credit: FurociTV Tyson Fury has asserted that there is a "one per cent" chance of his fight against Anthony Joshua going ahead. On Thursday, confirmation finally arrived that Fury and Joshua's all-British heavyweight showdown will take place at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on Friday December 11 following months of protracted negotiations to stage the biggest fight in British boxing history. Fury, though, cast doubt on the agreement on Saturday by claiming Joshua was trying to pull out of the fight, and has put his own estimate on the chances of the much-anticipated heavyweight bout going ahead.
